# eComChannels

> eComChannels is a multichannel commerce platform for online retailers: AI listing optimisation, AI graphics, AI auto shipping, a cloud order management system (OMS), finance auto reconciliation, AI social media outreach and branded storefronts.

Contact: support@ecomchannels.com
Full content for AI: https://ecomchannels.com/llms-full.txt
Agent guide: https://ecomchannels.com/agents.md
Sales channels ranked by company size: https://ecomchannels.com/channels/
Book a demo or a 30-day free trial: https://ecomchannels.com/book-a-demo/ (all products are currently on a 30-day free trial)

## Products
- [AI listing optimisation](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-listing-optimisation/): AI already trained on each marketplace’s listing rules writes titles, bullet points, descriptions and attributes, and your team approves them before they go live.
- [AI graphics](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-graphics/): AI already trained on every marketplace’s image rules produces product images, infographics and lifestyle shots, with one approval per image set.
- [AI auto shipping](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-shipping/): Book Australia Post, StarTrack, CouriersPlease and Allied Express from one screen, with labels, manifests and tracking sent back automatically.
- [Order management (OMS)](https://ecomchannels.com/products/order-management/): One queue for every order and one stock figure for every SKU, across all your marketplaces and stores.
- [Finance auto reconciliation](https://ecomchannels.com/products/finance-reconciliation/): Match every marketplace remittance and settlement to the orders it pays for, with fee rules, exceptions and finance reports.
- [AI social media outreach](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-social-media-marketing/): AI plans and writes posts for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X, Threads and RedNote, then publishes after approval.
- [Branded storefronts](https://ecomchannels.com/products/storefronts/): Your own fast, search-friendly web store, with products, prices and stock fed by the OMS.

## Channels
- Marketplaces (ranked by operator revenue): Amazon Australia (Amazon.com, Inc.), TikTok Shop (ByteDance Ltd (private)), Temu (Local Seller) (PDD Holdings Inc.), Woolworths Everyday Market (Woolworths Group), BIG W Market (Woolworths Group), MyDeal (Woolworths Group), Bunnings Marketplace (Wesfarmers Limited), Kmart Marketplace (Wesfarmers Limited), Decathlon Australia Marketplace (Decathlon Group), eBay Australia (eBay Inc.), JB Hi-Fi Marketplace (JB Hi-Fi Limited), Country Road Group Marketplace (Woolworths Holdings Limited (South Africa)), Velocity Frequent Flyer Store (Virgin Australia Holdings), Etsy (Etsy, Inc.), Myer Marketplace (Myer Holdings (Myer Group)), THE ICONIC Marketplace (Global Fashion Group), Lasoo (IVE Group), Temple & Webster (Temple & Webster Group), Baby Bunting Marketplace (Baby Bunting Group), Kogan Marketplace (Kogan.com Ltd)
- Web stores: Shopify, WooCommerce, eComChannels storefronts
- Couriers: Australia Post, StarTrack, CouriersPlease, Allied Express
- Social platforms: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X, Threads, RedNote (Xiaohongshu)

## Pages
- [AI tools that run your online retail, on every channel](https://ecomchannels.com/): AI listing optimisation, graphics, auto shipping, order management, reconciliation and social media for retailers on Amazon, eBay, Kogan and Bunnings.
- [eComChannels products](https://ecomchannels.com/products/): eComChannels products: AI listing optimisation, AI graphics, AI auto shipping, OMS, auto reconciliation, AI social media outreach and storefronts.
- [AI listing optimisation for every marketplace](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-listing-optimisation/): Listing AI already trained on each marketplace’s rules writes titles, bullets and descriptions for Amazon, Woolworths, BIG W, Bunnings, Kmart and more.
- [AI graphics for e-commerce and online retailers](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-graphics/): Graphics AI already trained on each marketplace’s image rules creates product images and infographics, with one approval for every channel.
- [AI auto shipping for Australian retailers](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-shipping/): Book Australia Post, StarTrack, CouriersPlease and Allied Express from one screen: labels, manifests and tracking sent to every channel automatically.
- [Multichannel order management system (OMS)](https://ecomchannels.com/products/order-management/): The eComChannels OMS brings orders, inventory, purchasing, pricing, B2B and customer service for every marketplace and web store into one system.
- [Finance auto reconciliation for marketplaces and online retailers](https://ecomchannels.com/products/finance-reconciliation/): Reconcile marketplace remittances and settlements against orders automatically, with fee rules and reports. Amazon, eBay, Kogan, Bunnings and more.
- [AI social media outreach on every major platform](https://ecomchannels.com/products/ai-social-media-marketing/): AI plans, writes and schedules posts for Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X, Threads and RedNote, with human approval.
- [Branded storefronts, connected to your OMS](https://ecomchannels.com/products/storefronts/): Your own branded online store on the eComChannels storefront engine: SEO and AI-search friendly, with products, prices and stock from the OMS.
- [Sales channels, couriers and platforms](https://ecomchannels.com/channels/): Australian online sales channels ranked by company size: Amazon, TikTok Shop, Temu, Woolworths, BIG W, Bunnings, Kmart, eBay, Myer, Lasoo and more.
- [Book a demo or start your 30-day free trial](https://ecomchannels.com/book-a-demo/): Book a live demo of eComChannels or start a 30-day free trial. Our team shows you AI listings, graphics, shipping, reconciliation and social media tools.
- [Frequently asked questions](https://ecomchannels.com/faq/): Answers about eComChannels products: AI listings, AI graphics, shipping couriers, OMS, marketplace reconciliation, social media and storefronts.
- [Contact eComChannels](https://ecomchannels.com/contact/): Contact eComChannels about AI listing optimisation, graphics, shipping, order management, reconciliation or social media. Email support@ecomchannels.com.
- [E-commerce insights](https://ecomchannels.com/insights/): 100 research-backed guides on what is changing in Australian e-commerce: marketplaces, AI listings, graphics, shipping, finance, social and AI search.
- [What the research says](https://ecomchannels.com/research/): Independent studies on how AI listings, product images, fast delivery, multichannel selling and automation lift visibility, traffic, sales and cut costs.

## Research findings (cited)
- 3-10%: THE ICONIC reports a 3-10% decrease in conversion for every additional day added to the delivery time shown at checkout. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 73%: 73% of Australian shoppers say a good delivery experience makes them more likely to shop online instead of in-store. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 4x: Customers using the AusPost tracking app are up to four times less likely to raise delivery-related cases during peak, reducing support costs. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 80%: When an item is out of stock, 80% of Australian online shoppers turn to a competitor. (Grant Thornton Australia, Value, Speed, and Reliability: What's Driving Australian Retail, 2025: https://www.grantthornton.com.au/globalassets/1.-member-firms/australian-website/industry/retail/pdfs/gtal_2026_retail_report.pdf)
- 35.26%: Large e-commerce sites can gain an average 35.26% increase in conversion rate by fixing documented checkout design issues. (Baymard Institute, Cart Abandonment Rate Statistics 2026, 2026: https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate)
- 23%: Pure online marketplaces captured $18.9 billion in 2025, 23% of all Australian online spending, making them the largest online category. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 48%: 48% of Australians have used AI when shopping online, mainly for price and product comparisons, so structured product data affects whether products are surfaced. (PayPal Australia, eCommerce Index 2026, 2026: https://www.paypalobjects.com/marketing/web24/au/PayPal_2026_eCommerce_Index_Infographic.pdf)
- 11%: Social media accounts for 11% of Australian online sales, and 67% of businesses now sell through social platforms. (IT Brief Australia, reporting PayPal eCommerce Index 2026, 2026: https://itbrief.com.au/story/australian-businesses-embrace-social-selling-paypal-says)
- 32%: 32% of Australian shoppers would choose one retailer over another if it offered out-of-home collection such as Parcel Lockers. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 26%: Online reached 26% of total Australian retail in the July-September 2026 quarter, with online spend up 17% year on year. (Australia Post, Quarterly eCommerce Update FY27 Q1, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost/documents/ecommerce/quarterly-updates/oct-2026-quarterly-ecommerce-update.pdf)
- 17.5x: Sellers active on two or more marketplaces averaged 17.5 times the GMV of sellers on a single marketplace ($10.07m vs $575,093). (Mirakl, The marketplace revolution: Key insights from our 2026 Seller Report, 2026: https://www.mirakl.com/blogs/brands-sellers/the-marketplace-revolution-key-insights-from-our-2026-seller-report/)
- 88%: Sellers using Mirakl's AI catalogue tool to classify products and standardise listings across marketplaces generated 88% higher GMV than those who did not (vendor-reported). (Mirakl, The marketplace revolution: Key insights from our 2026 Seller Report, 2026: https://www.mirakl.com/blogs/brands-sellers/the-marketplace-revolution-key-insights-from-our-2026-seller-report/)
- $18.9b: Australians spent $18.9 billion on pure online marketplaces in 2025, up 13% year on year and 23% of all online spending. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 29%: 29% of Australian shoppers start their product discovery on online marketplaces, so marketplace listings directly drive visibility. (Australia Post, Category Insights: Online marketplaces (eCommerce Report 2026), 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/australia-post-ecommerce-report-2026-online-marketplaces.pdf)
- 73%: 73% of Australian online shoppers made a purchase on a marketplace in 2025. (Australia Post, Category Insights: Online marketplaces (eCommerce Report 2026), 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/australia-post-ecommerce-report-2026-online-marketplaces.pdf)
- 26.7%: BIG W's eCommerce gross transaction value, including third-party marketplace sales, rose 26.7% to $956 million in F26, more than double the growth of its own online sales. (Woolworths Group, F26 Full Year Results Announcement, 2026: https://www.woolworthsgroup.com.au/content/dam/wwg/investors/asx-announcements/2026/3108623.pdf)
- 6.5%: Inventory distortion (out-of-stocks plus overstocks) costs retailers an estimated $1.73 trillion a year, 6.5% of global retail sales. (IHL Group, Retail Inventory Crisis Persists Despite $172 Billion in Improvements, 2025: https://www.ihlservices.com/news/analyst-corner/2025/09/retail-inventory-crisis-persists-despite-172-billion-in-improvements/)
- 5.5%: eBay Australia sellers rated Below Standard, for example through out-of-stock cancellations, pay an extra 5.5% fee on sales, rising to 6.6% after four months. (eBay Australia, eBay Pro selling fees, 2026: https://www.ebay.com.au/help/selling/fees-credits-invoices/ebay-stores-selling-fees-managed-payments-sellers?id=4809)
- 700+: Bunnings and Kmart marketplaces added more than 400,000 online SKUs and 700 sellers by June 2026, widening the retailer-led marketplace channel for third-party sellers. (Wesfarmers, 2026 Full-year results briefing presentation, 2026: https://links.sgx.com/FileOpen/WES26-022%202026%20Full-year%20results%20briefing%20presentation.ashx?App=Announcement&FileID=902523)
- 1.3 million: 1.3 million third-party sellers had used Amazon's generative AI listing tools, which Amazon says can produce about 70% of a product listing. (CNBC, Amazon introduces AI agent to help sellers with tedious tasks, 2025: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/17/amazon-ai-agent-sellers.html)
- 12 million+: Independent sellers created more than 12 million sales-ready listings using Amazon's generative AI in 2025. (About Amazon, A record number of independent sellers in Amazon's store surpassed $1 million in sales in 2025, 2026: https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/small-business/amazon-2025-small-business-empowerment-report)
- 8 hours to 1 hour: European small-business owners estimated AI could cut time spent writing product descriptions from an average of eight hours to one hour. (About Amazon EU, Amazon announces expansion of generative AI listing tools to sellers across Europe, 2024: https://www.aboutamazon.eu/news/empowering-small-business/amazon-announces-expansion-of-generative-ai-listing-tools-to-sellers-across-europe)
- 2.1x: eBay Australia says listing titles of 60 to 80 characters are 2.1 times more likely to sell. (eBay Australia Seller Centre, Listing an Item, 2026: https://www.ebay.com.au/sellercentre/private-selling/listing-an-item)
- 54%: 54% of shoppers dropped purchases because of conflicting product information. (Salsify, 2025 Consumer Research Report (press release), 2025: https://www.salsify.com/press-release-salsify-2025-consumer-research-report)
- 71%: 71% of shoppers have returned items over inaccurate product descriptions. (Salsify, 2025 Consumer Research Report (press release), 2025: https://www.salsify.com/press-release-salsify-2025-consumer-research-report)
- 44%: 44% of consumers have abandoned a purchase because of insufficient product information. (Syndigo, 2025 State of Product Experience Report, 2025: https://syndigo.com/news/2025-product-experience-report/)
- 62%: 62% of consumers say more accurate product information upfront would reduce their likelihood of making a return. (Akeneo, Akeneo Releases New Data Detailing Consumer Behavior & the Rationale Behind Product Returns, 2025: https://www.akeneo.com/press-release/akeneo-releases-new-data-detailing-consumer-behavior-the-rationale-behind-product-returns/)
- 41%: 41% of shoppers will scroll up to page three of search results to find the right product, so visibility beyond page one still drives traffic. (Salsify, 2025 Consumer Research Report (press release), 2025: https://www.salsify.com/press-release-salsify-2025-consumer-research-report)
- $18.9 billion: Australians spent $18.9 billion on pure online marketplaces in 2025, up 13% year on year and 23% of all online spending. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 76%: 76% of shoppers say high-quality product images are extremely or very important to their decision to click on a product page from search results. (Salsify, 2024 Consumer Research Report, 2024: https://www.salsify.com/hubfs/2024/Content/Salsify%20Consumer%20Research%20Report%202024.pdf)
- 45%: 45% of shoppers returned an item in the past year because of incorrect product content, such as images that didn't match the product. (Salsify, 2024 Consumer Research Report, 2024: https://www.salsify.com/hubfs/2024/Content/Salsify%20Consumer%20Research%20Report%202024.pdf)
- 40%: Placing a product in a lifestyle context in a mobile Sponsored Brands ad can deliver click-through rates 40% higher than ads with standard product images. (Amazon, Amazon rolls out AI-powered image generation to help advertisers, 2023: https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/innovation-at-amazon/amazon-ads-ai-powered-image-generator)
- 24%: Amazon product detail pages that added their first shoppable video saw an average 24% increase in sales compared with those without videos. (Amazon, Let Amazon product videos show customers what images can't, 2025: https://sell.amazon.com/blog/amazon-product-video)
- up to 20%: Basic A+ Content (enhanced images and comparison charts) can increase Amazon sales by up to 8%, and well-implemented Premium A+ Content by up to 20%. (Amazon, A+ Content, 2026: https://sell.amazon.com/tools/a-content)
- up to 94%: According to Shopify merchant data, products with AR and 3D content see conversion rates up to 94% higher than comparable products without them. (Shopify, 6 Digital Transformation Trends in Retail, 2026: https://www.shopify.com/au/blog/digital-transformation-trends-in-retail)
- 56%: 56% of users' first action on a product page is to explore the product images, before reading titles or descriptions. (Baymard Institute, Ensure Sufficient Image Resolution and Zoom, 2020: https://baymard.com/research-articles/ensure-sufficient-image-resolution-and-zoom)
- 37%: 42% of users try to gauge product size from images, yet 37% of sites provide no 'in scale' image. (Baymard Institute, Product Page UX 2026, 2026: https://baymard.com/research-articles/current-state-ecommerce-product-page-ux)
- 80%: 80% of surveyed users of Google's AI-powered Product Studio have been, or expect to be, more efficient creating product images and videos. (Google Merchant Center Help, About Product Studio, 2026: https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/13708167?hl=en)
- 73%: On 73% of mobile web pages the Largest Contentful Paint element is an image, so image delivery largely decides how fast a mobile page feels. (HTTP Archive, Web Almanac 2024: Performance, 2024: https://almanac.httparchive.org/en/2024/performance)
- 70%: 70% of shoppers say poor delivery communication at checkout makes them less likely to complete a purchase. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2026, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2026.pdf)
- 60%: Amazon says tracked orders have 60 per cent fewer order defects and that tracking helps reduce buyer enquiries. (Amazon Seller Central Australia, On-time delivery, 2026: https://sellercentral.amazon.com.au/help/hub/reference/external/G200847280)
- 39%: 39% of shoppers abandon a checkout because of additional fees such as delivery charges and taxes. (Baymard Institute, How to Reduce Cart Abandonment, 2026: https://baymard.com/blog/reduce-cart-abandonment)
- 3.5-4%: Australian retailers offering same- or next-day delivery grew 3.5 to 4% faster during Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025. (Shippit, Fast delivery won peak, 2025: https://www.shippit.com/delivered-newsletter/fast-delivery-won-peak)
- 60-70%: The last mile generates 60 to 70% of overall parcel delivery costs in a home delivery network, and raising parcels per stop from one to five can cut delivery costs by more than 50%. (McKinsey & Company, Out-of-Home Delivery: Mapping its evolution, 2024: https://www.mckinsey.com/de/publikationen/2024-10-28-ooh-delivery)
- 75%: 75% of shoppers say an easy returns process makes them more likely to buy again. (Australia Post, Trends and insights: Quarterly eCommerce Update, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/business/grow-your-business/trends-insights)
- 20%: Australia Post Parcel Locker usage grew 20% year on year, with more than two million registered users and locker returns up 36%. (Australia Post, Parcel Lockers in Australia: Locker Land insights, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/business/grow-your-business/business-ideas-blog/parcel-lockers-locker-land-merchant-host-insights)
- $18.9bn: Australians spent $18.9 billion through pure online marketplaces in 2025, up 13% year on year and almost a quarter of all online spending. (Australia Post, Why marketplaces are a powerful growth channel, 2026: https://auspost.com.au/business/grow-your-business/business-ideas-blog/marketplace-growth-strategy)
- 39%: Online marketplaces drove 39% of Australian online spend growth in 2024. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2025, 2025: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2025.pdf)
- 59%: 59% of accountants make several financial errors a month, and 18% make errors at least daily, with errors linked to capacity constraints. (Gartner, Survey Shows That a Third of Accountants Make Several Financial Errors Per Week due to Capacity Constraints, 2024: https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2024-02-21-gartner-survey-shows-that-a-third-of-accountants-make-several-error-per-weeo-due-to-capacity-constraints)
- 39%: 39% of finance functions using AI apply it to anomaly and error detection, and 44% to intelligent process automation. (Gartner, Survey Shows 58% of Finance Functions Using AI in 2024, 2024: https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2024-09-11-gartner-survey-shows-58-percent-of-finance-functions-use-ai-in-2024)
- 30%: A generative AI assistant for budget variance insights at a global consumer goods company saved an estimated 30% of finance professionals' time. (McKinsey & Company, How finance teams are putting AI to work today, 2025: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/strategy-and-corporate-finance/our-insights/how-finance-teams-are-putting-ai-to-work-today)
- 4.8 days: Top-quartile organisations complete the monthly close in 4.8 days or less, about half the time of the bottom quartile (10+ days); the median is 6.4 days. (CFO.com / APQC, Metric of the Month: Cycle Time for Monthly Close, 2018: https://www.cfo.com/news/metric-of-the-month-cycle-time-for-monthly-close/659297/)
- $128: Each chargeback costs merchants an average of $128 in third-party fees and internal costs, often more than the value of the disputed item. (Mastercard, What is the true cost of a chargeback for businesses?, 2025: https://www.mastercard.com/us/en/news-and-trends/Insights/2025/what-s-the-true-cost-of-a-chargeback-in-2025.html)
- 45%: 45% of Baby Boomer and Builder shoppers say they would abandon their cart and shop elsewhere if their preferred payment method was not offered. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2025, 2025: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2025.pdf)
- 20%: Online payments made up around 20% of all Australian consumer payments in 2025, up from 18% in 2022 and 4% in 2007. (Reserve Bank of Australia, Consumer Payment Behaviour in Australia, 2026: https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/bulletin/2026/may/pdf/consumer-payment-behaviour-in-australia.pdf)
- Most cited: Inadequate cash flow is the most cited cause of business failure among Australian company insolvencies. (Reserve Bank of Australia, Financial Stability Review April 2025: The Recent Increase in Company Insolvencies, 2025: https://www.rba.gov.au/publications/fsr/2025/apr/focus-topic-the-recent-increase-in-company-insolvencies-and-its-implications-for-financial-stability.html)
- $8 billion: Australian social commerce reached $4.9 billion in 2024 and is expected to grow to $8 billion by 2029. (Australia Post, eCommerce Report 2025, 2025: https://auspost.com.au/content/dam/auspost_corp/media/documents/ecommerce-reports/annual-ecommerce-reports/ecommerce-report-2025.pdf)
- 3 in 5: Three in five Australian shoppers have made a purchase on social media, and 53% say it could become their top shopping destination by 2030. (DHL eCommerce, Clicks, carts & conversions in Australia, 2025: https://www.dhl.com/content/dam/dhl/local/global/dhl-ecommerce/documents/pdf/g0-ecs-insights-country-report-australia-2025.pdf)
- 58%: More than 58% of Australians use social media for brand and product research, close to search engines (62%) and well ahead of brand websites (37%). (We Are Social, Digital 2025 Australia, 2025: https://wearesocial.com/au/blog/2025/02/digital-2025-australia-social-media-rivals-search-for-brand-discovery/)
- 5x: Highly consistent social posters received five times more engagement per post than inconsistent posters across more than 100,000 accounts. (Buffer, Consistent Posting Means 5x More Likes, Comments, and Shares, 2025: https://buffer.com/resources/consistent-posting-study/)
- 83%: 83% of social marketers say AI helps them create significantly more content. (Hootsuite, 60+ social media statistics marketers need to know in 2026, 2026: https://blog.hootsuite.com/social-media-statistics/)
- 270%: A product with five reviews had a 270% greater purchase likelihood than a product with no reviews. (Spiegel Research Center, How Online Reviews Influence Sales, 2017: https://spiegel.medill.northwestern.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2021/04/Spiegel_Online-Review_eBook_Jun2017_FINAL.pdf)
- 60%: 60% of Australian shoppers say customer reviews on social media influence their buying decisions. (DHL eCommerce, Clicks, carts & conversions in Australia, 2025: https://www.dhl.com/content/dam/dhl/local/global/dhl-ecommerce/documents/pdf/g0-ecs-insights-country-report-australia-2025.pdf)
- 80 billion: Pinterest sees over 80 billion searches a month, most of them visual, generating 1.7 billion monthly outbound clicks. (Pinterest, Q4 2025 earnings call transcript, 2026: https://s204.q4cdn.com/369458543/files/doc_financials/2025/q4/PINS-Q4-2025-Transcript.pdf)
- 75%: 75% of Australians aged 18 to 39 have discovered brand information from an influencer or content creator they follow. (IAB Australia, Australian and New Zealand Commerce Report 2025, 2025: https://www.iabaustralia.com.au/resource/ecommerce-report-2025/)
- 14%: Meta's average price per ad rose 14% year on year in Q3 2026, making organic reach and stronger creative more valuable. (exchange4media, Meta's ad revenue jumps 26% to $63 billion as AI boosts conversions, ad prices, 2026: https://www.exchange4media.com/digital-news/metas-ad-revenue-jumps-26-to-631-billion-as-ai-boosts-conversions-ad-prices-159351.html)
- 4-8%: Correcting inaccurate inventory records increased sales by about 4% to 8% across seven large retailers. (ECR Retail Loss / Cardiff University, Measuring the sales impact of improving inventory records, 2019: https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/142664/)
- 60%: About 60% of roughly one million SKUs analysed across around 100 stores had inventory record inaccuracies. (ECR Retail Loss / Cardiff University, Measuring the sales impact of improving inventory records, 2019: https://orca.cardiff.ac.uk/id/eprint/142664/)
- 95%+: Retailers using integrated platforms rather than scattered point tools achieve 95%+ inventory accuracy. (IHL Group research via British Retail Consortium, Fixing Inventory Distortion, 2025: https://brc.org.uk/news-and-events/news/associate-insight/2025/fixing-inventory-distortion-who-s-winning-who-s-failing-what-s-working/)
- 65% vs 55%: Smaller companies that automate report success more often than large ones (65% vs 55%). (McKinsey & Company, The imperatives for automation success, 2020: https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/operations/our-insights/the-imperatives-for-automation-success)
- 45%: Australian SMBs moving from basic to intermediate AI use are modelled to see a 45% increase in profitability. (Deloitte Access Economics, The AI edge for small business, 2025: https://www.deloitte.com/au/en/about/press-room/ai-edge-small-business-increased-smb-ai-adoption-can-add-44-billion-australias-economy-251125.html)
- 94%: 94% of SMB automation users report benefits, led by fewer errors (44%) and cost savings (44%). (Zapier, 76% of SMB owners are automating work, 2026: https://zapier.com/blog/ai-governance-for-small-teams/)

## FAQ
### What is eComChannels?
eComChannels is a multichannel commerce platform for online retailers. Its products cover AI listing optimisation, AI graphics, AI auto shipping, order management, finance auto reconciliation, AI social media outreach and branded storefronts, all working from the same product and order data.

### Which sales channels does eComChannels work with?
Amazon, TikTok Shop, Temu, Woolworths Everyday Market, BIG W Market, Bunnings Marketplace, Kmart Marketplace, eBay, Etsy, Myer Marketplace, THE ICONIC, Lasoo, Temple & Webster, Baby Bunting and Kogan, plus Shopify, WooCommerce and eComChannels storefronts. It also connects to every marketplace built on Mirakl, including Bunnings, Kmart, JB Hi-Fi, Myer, Country Road Group, Velocity, Decathlon, Baby Bunting, Freedom, Spotlight, Paramount Liquor, CampbellsPlus and Onceit, plus Mirakl marketplaces overseas. MyDeal closed in September 2025 and its sellers now trade on BIG W Market and Everyday Market.

### Which is the biggest online marketplace in Australia?
By the annual revenue of the company behind it, Amazon is the largest, followed by TikTok Shop (ByteDance), Temu (PDD Holdings), Woolworths Group (Everyday Market and BIG W Market) and Wesfarmers (Bunnings and Kmart marketplaces). The full ranking with sources is at https://ecomchannels.com/channels/.

### Do you support Mirakl marketplaces?
Yes. eComChannels connects to any marketplace built on Mirakl through the Mirakl seller API, using the shop API key the marketplace gives you. That covers 13 Mirakl marketplaces in Australia and New Zealand and more than 280 overseas. The full list is at https://ecomchannels.com/channels/#mirakl.

### Which couriers are supported?
Australia Post, StarTrack, CouriersPlease and Allied Express.

### Is there a free trial?
Yes. eComChannels products are currently available on a 30-day free trial. Book a demo or request a trial and our team will set you up and show you around.

### How do I book a demo?
Use the Book a demo page to tell us about your business and choose a preferred time. Our team will confirm the time and walk you through the products live.

### Can I use only one product?
Talk to us about the products you need. Each product works from the same central product and order data.

### How do I get started?
Book a demo or request your 30-day free trial at https://ecomchannels.com/book-a-demo/, or email support@ecomchannels.com.

### Which marketplaces is the listing AI trained for?
It is already trained on the listing rules of Amazon, TikTok Shop, Temu, Woolworths Everyday Market, BIG W Market, Bunnings Marketplace, Kmart Marketplace, eBay, Etsy, Myer Marketplace, THE ICONIC, Lasoo, Temple & Webster, Baby Bunting and Kogan, plus Shopify, WooCommerce and eComChannels storefronts.

### Does AI publish listings automatically?
No. The AI drafts to each marketplace’s trained rules, and a person on your team approves them before they are published.

### How does eComChannels handle different marketplace image rules?
Each marketplace is mapped to an image set that holds its slot rules. Designers produce images to the set, and approval publishes them to every channel that uses it.

### Can AI create product images?
Yes. The graphics AI, already trained on each marketplace’s image rules, generates and edits product graphics, and every image is reviewed before it is approved for a channel.

### Which couriers does eComChannels shipping support?
Australia Post, StarTrack, CouriersPlease and Allied Express.

### Is tracking sent to marketplaces automatically?
Yes. Once a shipment is labelled, its tracking number is sent back to the customer and to the marketplace or store the order came from.

### What does an order management system (OMS) do?
An OMS collects orders from every place you sell, keeps one accurate stock figure per product and runs fulfilment, with tracking sent back to each sales channel.

### Does eComChannels prevent overselling?
Stock is held centrally per SKU and the available quantity is pushed to each connected channel, so a sale on one marketplace reduces what is offered on the others.

### What does marketplace reconciliation mean?
Checking that every order sold on a marketplace was paid for, at the right amount after commission and fees, by matching remittance or settlement lines to orders.

### Which channels can be reconciled?
Any marketplace or store whose remittance or settlement report can be imported, including Amazon, Temu, Woolworths Everyday Market, BIG W Market, Bunnings Marketplace, Kmart Marketplace, eBay, Etsy, Myer Marketplace, THE ICONIC, Lasoo, Temple & Webster, Baby Bunting and Kogan and Shopify.

### Which social media platforms does eComChannels support?
Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, X, Threads and RedNote (Xiaohongshu).

### Does AI post without approval?
No. AI drafts and schedules posts, and each one is approved by a person before it is published.

### Can I run my own online store with eComChannels?
Yes. The storefront engine powers branded web stores with server-rendered, search-friendly pages, and products, prices and stock come straight from the OMS.
